record.paper_title: Progress and open questions in the physics of neutrino cross sections at intermediate energies
record.original_question: How can the axial mass M_A be extracted reliably from quasielastic neutrino data on nuclear targets once nuclear dynamics, multinucleon excitations, and other model-dependent corrections are taken into account, so that the extracted value is not an artifact of the chosen nuclear model?

evidence.quote: The model dependence in the determination of MA in experiments with nuclear targets, in the light of new theoretical developments, is discussed in Sec. III.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In neutrino–nucleus quasielastic charged-current scattering, the hadronic vertex is parameterized in terms of the nucleon axial form factor, conventionally taken in the dipole form
F_A(Q^2) = g_A / (1 + Q^2/M_A^2)^2,
where g_A ≈ 1.27 is fixed by neutron beta decay and M_A > 0 is the axial mass parameter. When this elementary vertex is embedded in a nuclear target, the measured inclusive double-differential cross section dσ/(dT_μ dcosθ_μ) receives contributions not only from one-body quasielastic scattering on bound nucleons (modeled, e.g., via a relativistic Fermi gas, a spectral function, or a continuum random-phase-approximation treatment) but also from two-body and multinucleon mechanisms such as meson-exchange currents, short-range correlations, and 2p2h excitations, as well as from final-state interactions and binding/Pauli-blocking effects.

Devise a procedure for extracting M_A from a given set of inclusive quasielastic-like cross-section measurements on nuclear targets that satisfies the following criteria:

(a) The procedure must incorporate, in a controlled way, the contributions of multinucleon excitations and other nuclear-medium corrections together with the genuine one-body quasielastic process.

(b) The extracted central value and uncertainty for M_A must be demonstrably stable with respect to the choice among physically admissible nuclear models (Fermi gas, spectral function, RPA-based, etc.), in the sense that the resulting confidence intervals overlap and the central value does not shift by more than the quoted theoretical uncertainty.

(c) The procedure must reproduce, within stated uncertainties, the value of M_A obtained from neutrino–deuteron and pion electroproduction data, so that the extracted M_A can be interpreted as an intrinsic nucleon property rather than as an effective parameter absorbing unmodeled nuclear effects.

Construct such a procedure, or prove that no procedure satisfying (a)–(c) exists with currently available theoretical inputs and data.
artifact.status_search_result: The reliable, model-independent extraction of the axial mass M_A from quasielastic neutrino-nucleus data remains an open problem. Different nuclear models (relativistic Fermi gas, spectral function, RPA, models including 2p2h/MEC) continue to yield mutually inconsistent values of M_A, and recent works (e.g. Phys. Rev. D 84, 073006 (2011); Phys. Rev. D 92, 113011 (2015); EPJC 2021 "running axial mass") propose partial remedies but none has produced a fully model-independent consensus value. The discrepancy between higher M_A values fit to MiniBooNE-like data on carbon and the lower deuterium/electroproduction value persists.

status_evidence.title: Model independent determination of the axial mass parameter in quasielastic neutrino-nucleon scattering
status_evidence.snippet: A model-independent description of the axial-vector form factor was presented, analyzing MiniBooNE data under a definite nuclear model assumption.
status_evidence.claim: Attempts at model-independent extraction depend on the assumed nuclear model and yield M_A values inconsistent with traditional dipole fits.

status_evidence.title: Extraction of the axial mass parameter from MiniBooNE neutrino quasielastic double differential cross-section data, Phys. Rev. C 82, 045502 (2010)
status_evidence.snippet: More restrictive q-cuts give smaller fitted M_A; Fermi gas and spectral function models give different values.
status_evidence.claim: Extracted M_A depends sensitively on cuts and nuclear-model choice.

status_evidence.title: Running axial mass of the nucleon as a phenomenological tool, EPJC 2021
status_evidence.snippet: Phenomenological 'running' M_A is introduced to accommodate inconsistent extractions across experiments and targets.
status_evidence.claim: The community still treats M_A as effectively process- and target-dependent, indicating the extraction problem is unresolved.
